sources.citation: Takata, Masahiro & Yuko Takata. 1992. Kola phonology. In Donald A. Burquest & Wyn D. Laidig (eds.), Descriptive studies in languages of Maluku (NUSA 34), 31-46. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya.
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE KOLA (kola1285), Kolamar/Marlasi villages, not Kompane. Sec. 2.5 p. 40: 'It is not predictable whether stress occurs on the penultimate or the ultimate syllable of monomorphemic words. Penultimate stress, however, is most common in Kola. It should be noted that stress falls only on the root and never on affixes or clitics. In addition, stress does not occur beyond the penult of the root.' Gives minimal pairs (/'bobah/ 'fear' vs /bo'bo/ 'baby'); stress shifts under resyllabification in compounds; Sec. 4 p. 43 defines the phonological word as a stress group with one primary stre…

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.2.3.3 (p. 98): Kompane spoken by 254 people in one village (Kompane, east coast of Kongan Island); no dialect variation; relates to the nearest Kola village Mohang Sel at 79% and is a 'bridge' between Ujir/Kola and the central Aru chain. Lexicostatistics only.
